figures.caption: Table 1. Variance in human RTs explained by grouping models. Human RT data are from Adeli et al.22. Among the models presented here, the GammaNet is the only neural network that groups regions directly in natural images. Adeli et al.22 derived processing times from affinities between image regions in pretrained DNN representations and Adeli et al. 48 trained a read-out network on self-supervised transformer features to predict human RTs directly; the remaining models operated on contour-only stimuli (Fig. 3D). Values are explained variance with 95% confidence intervals. P-values are from Z-tests comparing each estimate with the four-scale GammaNet, which served as the reference model. For each model with several trained instances (all except the Growth-Cone model), the best instance is shown; all models were evaluated on the same trials.
